Publish the database as parquet tranches, fetch only what a spec needs

Source: R/md-tranches.R
md_publish_tranches.Rd

The database is one 11.7 GB file, but a custom spec reads a small part of it. md_publish_tranches() writes the database as parquet files, split so that a spec can name the files it needs (PLAN.md section 7b, tier 2). md_fetch_tranches() downloads those files and no others. md_tranche_db() opens them as a connection that md_compile(), md_publish() and the lookup functions take in place of md_db().

Usage

md_publish_tranches(
  con = NULL,
  root = md_path("tranches"),
  tables = NULL,
  commit = NA_character_,
  set_latest = TRUE
)

md_tranche_pointer(build, root = md_path("tranches"))

md_fetch_tranches(
  spec = NULL,
  tables = NULL,
  build = NULL,
  remote = md_remote(),
  root = md_path("tranches"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

md_tranche_db(build = NULL, root = md_path("tranches"), verify = TRUE)

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

root

The tranche directory. Defaults to md_data_root()/tranches.

tables

Tables to publish. The default is every table except the observation ledger, which only maintainer code reads.

commit

The matchdb commit the database was built from, recorded in the manifest.

set_latest

Point latest.json at this build.

build

A build id, e.g. "2026-10-27-1a2b3c4d". By default the one latest.json names.

spec

An md_spec(): fetch the files md_compile() needs for it.

remote

The base URL of a matchdb copy; tranches are under <remote>/tranches/.

overwrite

Download again even when a file is already here and intact.

verify

Check every local file against its md5 before opening it.

Value

md_publish_tranches(): the build directory, invisibly.

md_fetch_tranches(): the local build directory, invisibly.

md_tranche_db(): a DBI connection.

Details

md_fetch_tranches() takes a spec, a set of tables, or both. tables names whole tables ("orgtext", "ein_relation", ...); naming "name" or "address" takes every partition with its derived columns, and "all" takes everything. With neither, it takes everything. entity and source_vintage always come along. Files already here and intact are not downloaded again, so fetching for a second spec adds only what the first did not need.

md_tranche_db() opens an in-memory DuckDB holding one view per table, over whichever files are here. A spec whose files are not all here is an error from md_compile() naming them, never a reference built from part of the data. Close it with md_db_close().

The layout

A build is <root>/<build>/, and <root>/latest.json names the current one. The build directory holds:

name/<layer>/<variant_class>.parquet

the name rows of one layer and class, sorted by EIN

name_derived/<layer>/<variant_class>.parquet

their derived columns, split the same way

address/..., address_derived/...

the same for addresses

tables/<table>.parquet

every other table, whole, sorted by EIN where it has one

manifest.json

the build id, the normalizer signature, the database fingerprint, and for every file its table, layer, class, rows, bytes and md5

Derived columns are separate files rather than joined in: address and address_derived both have zip5 and is_po_box, with different meanings, and separate files keep every table exactly as it is in the database.

Why layer and class, and not band

Layers partition EINs, and every spec selects by layer and by class, so a file per layer and class lets a spec skip what it does not select. The corroboration band is not split out: most of the 32 statistics cells are small (several under ten rows), and a file per cell would add a download per cell for no gain.

What a spec needs

md_compile() decides each name's class across every class of the selected EINs before it applies the spec's class filter, so a spec needs all of its layers' name files except in-care-of names, which compile never reads. It needs only the address classes it selects. It also needs entity, source_vintage, the three statistics tables and the two cluster tables. Historical addresses (the largest address class, and in no published tier) are downloaded only by a spec that selects them.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# maintainer: write the tranches from a built database
md_publish_tranches()

# user: download what one spec needs, and compile it
sp <- md_spec(layers = "bmf_active", names = c("legal", "dba"))
md_fetch_tranches(sp)
con <- md_tranche_db()
r <- md_compile(sp, con)
md_db_close(con)
} # }
